title: 3D Animated Ad Cost and Timeline: Published Prices for 2026
summary: What a 3D animated ad costs and how long it takes, with published studio prices, per-second math, turnaround times and when a done-for-you route fits.
body_markdown:
A 3D animated ad costs whatever the studio quotes for the finished piece, and few studios publish a number. Vidico lists 3D animation at $5,000 to $50,000+ per minute, B2W's animated commercials start from $2,400 for 60 seconds, and timelines run from about two weeks with a rush fee to roughly two months for a custom project. If you need 3D character ads in weekly batches rather than one commercial, Knowlify is the done-for-you route we recommend, on a custom quote. Knowlify publishes this guide and sells one of the services compared.


## What does a 3D animated ad cost from a studio?


Each published price buys a different unit, so read the table by the column that says what the price covers. As of October 2026, these are the figures in this comparison:


Provider Published price What the price buys Turnaround


Knowlify (our top pick) Custom quote Weekly batches of 3D character, AI UGC and AI commercial ads First batch on day 5, across formats


[B2W](https://www.b2w.tv/services/animated-commercial-video-production) From $2,400; the page does not name a style and says 3D carries higher production costs One 60-second animated commercial with script, voiceover and sound design 4 to 6 weeks, or 2 to 3 with a rush fee


[Vidico](https://vidico.com/services/animation-video-production/) 3D at $5,000 to $50,000+ per minute; monthly plans from around $5,000 Per-minute projects covering modeling, texturing and rendering, or a flat monthly plan covering video, design and animation No durations published; depends on length, 2D or 3D and revision rounds


[Superside](https://www.superside.com/pricing) $15,000 monthly minimum on an annual term, with a $1,000 monthly software fee A creative subscription whose flexible budget covers specialist production including motion, 3D and video editing Not stated


[Creatify Studio](https://creatify.ai/studio) $100 to $200 per video, per its Studio page AI-produced video ads, not 3D animation, shown as an AI-route reference point 48 hours


[Yum Yum Videos](https://www.yumyumvideos.com/) Not published Custom 2D, motion graphics, whiteboard and mixed media explainers 7 to 9 weeks for most projects


Two things move a quote more than runtime does: how many cutdowns you need, and what the price includes. B2W includes square, vertical 9:16 and social-cut formats in every project, plus two revision rounds at the script, storyboard and animation stages. Vidico says one project can be cut into hooks, ad variations and social posts. Ask every provider to price the cutdowns on their own line, and ask whether the Superside software fee sits inside the $15,000 minimum or on top of it.


## How much do studios charge per second for 3D ads?


Almost no studio quotes per second, so the figures above are per project, per minute or per month. You can still divide them for a rough scale. Every number below is our arithmetic from a published price:


- **Vidico 3D:** $5,000 to $50,000+ per minute works out to about $83 to $833+ a second. Its FAQ ties the 3D range to modeling, texturing and rendering.
- **Vidico 2D, for comparison:** $1,500 to $20,000+ per minute works out to about $25 to $333+ a second. The same FAQ adds that most B2B explainers land between $5,000 and $12,000 per minute, or about $83 to $200 a second.
- **B2W:** $2,400 for 60 seconds is about $40 a second at the starting price. B2W does not say which style that price covers and notes that 3D carries higher production costs, so a 3D quote may land above it.


A per-second figure hides the work the price buys. A fee covers concepting, scripting, revisions and every cutdown, and a single 60-second film cut into three lengths is still one concept. Price the finished ads in each size you need, and ask whether the character and scene builds are a one-time cost that later ads reuse. That answer decides whether a weekly series gets cheaper per ad or stays expensive.


## How long does it take to make a 3D animated ad?


A hand-built studio piece takes weeks, and an AI-made batch can start within days. The published timelines differ in scope, so read each one against the deliverable it covers.


- **B2W:** most projects take 4 to 6 weeks from brief to final file, or 2 to 3 weeks with a rush fee.
- **Vidico:** it publishes no durations. Its FAQ says timelines depend on the video's length, whether it is 2D or 3D, and how many revision rounds you want, and a producer maps the schedule at kickoff.
- **Yum Yum Videos:** most custom explainer projects take 7 to 9 weeks, and rush production is available.
- **351 Studio:** as of October 2026, its[AI video production page](https://351studio.com/ai-video-production) describes generative AI with human creative direction, and 351 Studio lists a 2 to 12 business day turnaround depending on scope.
- **Knowlify:** the first batch lands on day 5, and about 25 finished ads a week follow. That timing covers all three formats, and we do not publish a separate 3D turnaround.


Studio timelines run in stages. B2W's two revision rounds sit at the script, storyboard and animation stages, and Vidico describes its process as running from script and storyboard to final render, so the clock includes each sign-off. Ask whether the turnaround starts at brief approval or at kickoff, because that changes the date you can plan around.
